summary: Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Jochem Schindler, Heiner Eichner, and at the universities of Vienna (PhD c. 1992–1996) and Zurich. He held positions at the University of Zurich (1995) and the University of Münster (2002).

Michael Jansen (1947–2022) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist educated at Bonn, RWTH Aachen, Rome, and Delhi. He served as dean of architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999), founding rector at the German University of Technology in Oman (2007–2008), and president of the Research Centre Indian Ocean.

Michael K. Jerryson (1974–2021) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. An undergraduate alumnus of the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under Harold Scheub, he later held posts at Eckerd College (attested 2010) and Youngstown State University (attested 2016).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter (1947–2020) was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry Moses. He was affiliated with Indiana University as an editorial consultant (1982) and cataloger (2020), and Lumbini International Research Institute (2000).
Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.

Michael Oppitz is a scholar in Tibetology. He held an appointment at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin from around 1987 to 1988 and served as director (Leiter) at the University of Zurich from approximately 1991 to 2008.
Michael P. Berman is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (c. 1986–1994) under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and joined Harvard University around 1994.

Michael Pye is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Cambridge and Leeds, and held appointments at the University of Leeds (c. 1971–1978), University of Marburg (1982–2004), Lancaster University (1991–1994), and Otani University (c. 2006–2007).

Michael Radich specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After doctoral studies at Harvard (c. 2001–2007) and further study at Kyoto University (2009), he held faculty appointments at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and the University of Heidelberg (from 2018).

Michael Rostovtzeff (1870–1952) was a historian-archaeologist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Kyiv and St. Petersburg, he held posts at St. Petersburg University, Bestuzhev Courses, Oxford (1918–1920), University of Wisconsin-Madison (1920–1925), and Yale University (1925–1939).
Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1979, 1992, attested 2008) and worked on the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland in 1992.

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies. He held positions at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019).

Michael Silverstein (1945–2020) was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (c. 1962–1972). He spent his academic career at the University of Chicago from around 1970 until 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. His posts include Nanyang Technological University, University of Pittsburgh, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and University of Leipzig.
Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held an appointment as a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was a Danish scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, he served there as assistant librarian (1861) and as professor of Indian philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Harvard University (BA 1964, MA 1971, PhD 1974) and the University of Pennsylvania, he has served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania since circa 1976.
